Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed against the award passed   the Workmen Compensation Commissioner/Deputy Commissioner of  Labour-1 at Chennai, dated 12.02.2009 in W.C. No.170 of 2007.
 For Appellants : Mr.T. Deeraj  For Respondents : No Appearance for R1 & R2  : Mr. Michael Viswasam for R3  *****

This appeal arose from the award passed by the Workmen Compensation Commissioner/Deputy Commissioner of Labour-1 at Chennai, dated 12.02.2009 in W.C. No.170 of 2007 is filed by the applicants challenging the award, mainly on the ground that the Insurance Company/3rd respondent is exonerated from the liability to pay the compensation to the claimants/petitioners.

The appellants herein are the petitioners and the respondents herein are the respondents-Opposite Parties in W.C. No.170 of 2007 on the file of the Deputy Commissioner of Labour-I, Chennai.
The 1st appellant is the wife and 2nd and 3rd appellants are the daughters and 4th and 5th appellants are the mother and father respectively, and being legal heirs of the deceased Sundarakesavan.

3. The case of the appellants herein is that Sundarakesavan, the husband of the 1st petitioner /1st appellant herein, died on 10.01.2007 owing to the severe injuries sustained in the accident occurred o n 2 7 . 1 2 . 2 0 0 6 w h i l e h e w a s e m p l o y e d a s a A u t o D r i v e r w i t h A . R a m e s h , 2 n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent herein.

As the said Accident took place during the course of employment, the legal heirs of the deceased, filed an Application in W.C.No.170 of 2007 before the Deputy Commissioner of Labour-I, Chennai, (hereinafter referred to as "the Commissioner") claiming compensation under Section 10 of the Workmen's Compensation Act.

The Insurance Company filed its Counter stating that if there was a valid insurance, the same was not transferred duly to the 2nd respondent who is said to be the owner of the Vehicle and also questioning the relationship between the deceased Sundarakesavan and the 2nd respondent herein.

The Commissioner after hearing parties and perusing the documents brought on record, passed an award of Rs.3,52,980/-(Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand Nine Hundred and Eighty Only) to the petitioners/appellants herein by fastening the liability only on the 2nd respondent and relieving the Insurance Company/3rd respondent herein from the liability holding that after the 1st respondent herein had sold his Vehicle to the 2nd respondent herein, the Insurance Policy was not transferred to the name of the 2nd respondent herein and stood in the name of 1st respondent.
Being aggrieved by the said award of the Commissioner, the petitioners/appellants herein have filed the present Civil Miscellaneous Appeal to set aside the same.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.The learned counsel for the appellants would submit that the Commissioner has specifically held that the 1st appellant's husband died due to the accident during the course of employment and the Insurance Policy was valid from 09.01.2006 to 08.09.2007 at the time of the accident ie. 27.12.2006 thereby the Commissioner ought to have saddled the liability on the respondent 2 and 3 jointly.
The Commissioner ought not to have exonerated the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company merely because, the Insurance Policy under Ex.P3 was still in the name of the 1st respondent herein.

Despite the 1st respondent sold the said vehicle to the 2nd respondent, the documents in respect of the said vehicle were also transferred in the name of the 2nd respondent and further there was a valid policy from 09.01.2006 to 08.09.2007 at the time of accident.

While being so, as per Section 157(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased even the Insurance policy is not transferred to the 2nd respondent herein.

However, the Commissioner has erred in holding that the 2nd respondent herein alone is liable to pay the compensation amount without considering the fact that the Insurance Company/3rd respondent herein is also equally liable to pay the claim amount under Section 157(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Dhanasekari @ Dhakshayani vs S. Velu on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139416571/
2 5.

In support of his contentions, the learned counsel for the appellants has placed reliance of Judgment of the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam passed in the case of "Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Ors. Vs. Annamma Raju and Ors." reported in Manu/KE/3180/2022 wherein it has been observed as follows:
"15..... Section 157(1) of the Act clearly contemplates a deemed transfer, the moment the vehicle is transferred to a third person.

entities.text: High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Ors. Vs. Annamma Raju and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, what could be gathered from the aforesaid provision is that once a transfer is affected by following the procedure contemplated in the Motor Vehicles Act, the certificate of insurance is deemed to have been transferred in favour of the transferee without any further process.

.... Therefore, it is clear that, as far as the non- compliance with Section 157(2) is concerned, it will have no consequence as regards the liability of the Insurance company to indemnify the insured in respect of the claims arising from the victims of the Motor Vehicle Accident.
20. The policy of insurance is issued in respect of the vehicle, though it is issued in the name of the owner of the vehicle.
... Therefore, a change of name of the owner of the vehicle, cannot have any consequences, as far as the said coverage is concerned.
This is because, identity of the owner is not at all material for the said purpose, as the policy is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis issued for the vehicle.

Such a change of ownership would not have any impact on the insurable interest as per the policy,
because of the reason that, in the case of third party coverage, the insurable interest is not that of the owner, but it is for the third parties, who are the victims of the accidents.
Therefore, on this ground also, the contentions of the Insurance company is liable to be rejected."

Further, relying on the Judgment rendered in "Sayed Vs. Gopalakrishnan and Ors. reported in MANU/KE/0192/2016, the learned counsel for the appellants referred to the observations made therein as follows:
7..... Under Section 157 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 there is a deemed transfer and merely because the insurned die not inform the transfer to the insurer, that will not absolve the insurer from the liability to pay compensation unless they were able to prove the defence available under Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

entities.text: Sayed Vs. Gopalakrishnan and Ors. reported in MANU/KE/0192/2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid observations made by the High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam, the Insurance Company is also liable to pay the compensation to the appellants herein.

entities.text: High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam

sentences.text: 6. The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company has not objected the contention raised by the appellants and further he also https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis agreed that the Insurance Company/3rd respondent is also liable to pay the compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased under Section 157(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

Accordingly, he has placed reliance of the Judgment in the case of "Mallamma (Dead) by L.Rs. Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. and Dhanasekari @ Dhakshayani vs S. Velu on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139416571/
3 others", reported in 2014 ACJ 1266 wherein it has been observed as follows:
15.In view of the above discussion we are of the considered view that as on the date of accident, the decease workman was in the course of employment of Jeeva Rathina Setty in whose name the ownership of the vehicle stood transferred and the said vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy, the High Court ought not to have simply brushed aside the decision of the Commissioner fastening joint liability on the insurance company in the light of the deeming provision contained in section 157(1)
of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, he has relied upon the Judgment in the case of "Firdaus Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others" wherein it has been observed as follows:
16.

sentences.text: In view of the above, it is not necessary for us to give any concluded finding regarding ownership of the Vehicle No.HR- 2-G-1875 on the date of accident for the purpose of this case.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

In either of the eventuality, ie. whether defendant No.1 was the owner of the vehicle on the date of the accident or defendant No.4 was the owner of the vehicle, the liability of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd, contiunes and Workmen's compensation Commissioner has rightly fastened the liability on the insurance company.
The remand made by the High Court to find out as to whether Parvez Khan was an employee of the defendant No.1 or not was unnecessary.
7. Heard, the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent as well as perused the materials available on record.
Despite notice served and paper publication effected in the news papers, there is no representation on the side of the respondents 1 and 2 and hence they remained ex-parte.

8. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions of the learned counsel for parties, on the date of accident ie. 27.12.2006, even though the vehicle stood transferred from the insured and the Insurance Policy was not transferred in the name of the 2nd respondent, the Insurance Policy was a valid one from 09.01.2006 to 08.09.2007.

As per Section 157(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, -Transfer of certificate of insurance contemplates as follows:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis "Where a person in whose favour the certificate of insurance has been issued in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter transfer to another person the ownership of the motor vehicle in respect of which such insurance was taken together with the policy of insurance relating thereto, the certificate of insurance and the policy described in the certificate shall be deemed to have been transferred in favour of the person to whom the motor vehicle is transferred with effect from the date of transfer."

In view of the aforesaid fact, the the certificate of insurance and the policy described in the certificate shall be deemed to have been transferred in favour of the 2nd Dhanasekari @ Dhakshayani vs S. Velu on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139416571/
4 respondent.
9.

Further, as per the observation made in the Judgment in the case of "Firdaus Vs.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others" there is no necessity to find out whether the deceased was an employee with the 2nd respondent herein.

Firdaus Vs.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
wherein it has been observed as follows:
16.

In view of the above, it is not necessary for us to give any concluded finding regarding ownership of the Vehicle No.HR- https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2-G-1875 on the date of accident for the purpose of this case.

In either of the eventuality, ie. whether defendant No.1 was the owner of the vehicle on the date of the accident or defendant No.4 was the owner of the vehicle, the liability of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd, contiunes and Workmen's compensation Commissioner has rightly fastened the liability on the insurance company.
The remand made by the High Court to find out as to whether Parvez Khan was an employee of the defendant No.1 or not was unnecessary.

In view of the above, this Court is of the view that as on the date of accident, the deceased workman was in the course of employment of the 2nd respondent in whose name the ownership of the vehicle stood transferred and the said vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy.

At any event, even whether the 1st respondent was the owner of the vehicle on the date of accident as per the Insurance Policy or the 2nd respondent was the owner of the said vehicle as per the Registration Certificate

,
the liability of Insurance Company continues.

Hence, the Workmen's Compensation Commissioner committed an error by not fastening liability on the Insurance Company/3rd respondent herein without considering the provision contained in Section 157(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act.

Hence, the Insurance Company/3rd respondent herein is also liable to pay the compensation of Rs.3,52,980/-(Rupees Three Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Nine Hundred and Eighty Only) to the claimants/appellants as awarded by the Commissioner.
The Insurance Company/3rd respondent herein is hereby directed to pay the compensation to the claimants/appellants herein as awarded by the Commissioner.
10. In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands allowed by setting aside the Award date 12.02.2009 in W.C. No.170 of 2007 passed by the Deputy Commissioner of Labour-I, Chennai.
There shall be no order as to costs.
